failures.criterion: Item 8 / items 1-2: a mention sent during a listener take-over reaches its session once (no double delivery)
failures.evidence: Red test TestACommentDuringAListenerTakeOverReachesTheRouteHolderOnce (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/comment_mention_takeover_test.go, commit d71c537c493b). Command: `cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:55432/postgres?sslmode=disable go test -count=1 -v -run TestACommentDuringAListenerTakeOverReachesTheRouteHolderOnce ./internal/dispatch/api/` -> FAIL 'session s1 received the comment 2 times, want once: 1 mention steer(s) and 1 route fan-out(s); comment.created suppress_route=false while the mention's delivery is [session:s1 attempt 1 sent to s1]'. Cause: the pre-commit mention resolution fails during the take-over (comment_delivery.go:46-60), so resolveCommentRoute (comment_create.go:278-281) and suppressRoute/suppressedAuthors (comment_create.go:418-441) leave the route fan-out on; the post-commit take-over retry then resolves and sends the mention to s1 (comment_delivery.go:483-499, envoy_resolve.go:187-190), and the outbox fans the comment to s1 as the route holder too (outbox/publisher.go:417, :891-899), under a different key. Before item 8 the mention settled failed at once, so s1 got one copy.

Command as above with -run TestACommentMentioningSeveralEndedSessionsAnswersWithinOneTakeOverWindow -> FAIL 'the comment mentioning 2 ended sessions answered after 23.6s, want within 14s'. createCommentFor sends each mention in turn before it answers (comment_create.go:666-674) and each ended-session mention waits out listenerTakeoverWindow (envoy_resolve.go:161); up to 10 mentions are allowed (comment_create.go:63), so 5+ ended or unreachable mentions pass packages/envoy-client/src/dispatch-http.ts's 60 s AbortSignal after the comment committed, and the CLI's retry posts the comment again (new comment id, new mention keys, duplicate frames to the live mentioned sessions).

failures.criterion: Item 6 caches: the repositories cache with its 10-minute TTL keeps each caller's own request independent (base looked up on each caller's own context)
failures.evidence: Red test TestOneCallersCancellationDoesNotFailAnotherCallersRepositoryToken (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/githubapp/repository_token_cancel_test.go, commit a83e31fc2c9b). Command: `... go test -count=1 -v -run TestOneCallersCancellationDoesNotFailAnotherCallersRepositoryToken ./internal/dispatch/githubapp/` -> FAIL 'the second caller's RepositoryToken(acme/web) = ("", GET https://github.test/repos/acme/web/installation: ... context canceled), want its token'. RepositoryToken's loader closure (githubapp/client.go:478-481) captures the first caller's ctx and ttlCache.get shares it through singleflight (client.go:178-201), so a browser navigating away fails every concurrent caller for that repository (githubapi/proxy.go turns it into 502 GITHUB_UPSTREAM; a reconcile or intake fetch fails its pass). The TTL makes the cold path recur every 10 minutes per repository.

observations: Not failures, for the reviewer: (a) a person's Retry while the request's own send waits out a take-over opens attempt 2 beside the renewed attempt 1 (message_delivery.go:456-466, comment_delivery.go:247-252), the existing rule the implementer kept (implement.json trickyParts); the window that rule applies in grows from ~5 s to ~12-17 s, and a Retry in another mode sends a second frame under another key.
